title: The quasi-isometry classes of Galton–Watson trees: Lean formalisation
abstract: Lean 4 formalisation of the automorphism-matching theorems and the quasi-isometry classification of Galton–Watson trees from the paper "The quasi-isometry classes of Galton–Watson trees" by Jayadev S. Athreya and Sascha Troscheit (arXiv:2609.23882). The audited statements are: the i.i.d. matching theorem on the binary tree (leaf and full bounds, and the existence of a root-fixing automorphism of the infinite binary tree matching two independent i.i.d. labellings with probability at least 1 - 16 η_{5/2}, where η_{5/2} is the one-site potential of the label law); the general Markov matching theorem for typed label processes on the binary tree, in its finite-type and zero-compatible forms at finite and at infinite height, with a failure probability at most a constant multiple of the one-site defect; the complete classification, up to quasi-isometry, of Galton–Watson trees with finitely supported offspring law conditioned on infinite diameter, into the ray class, the binary-tree class, one chain class for each branching semigroup, and the bushy class, with two independent conditioned trees almost surely quasi-isometric exactly when their laws share a class, together with the finite class, so that over the unconditioned laws two trees are almost surely quasi-isometric exactly when both are finite or both are infinite with laws in the same class; the mutual embeddability theorem, that a Galton–Watson tree with finitely supported supercritical offspring law, conditioned on infinite diameter, almost surely admits quasi-isometric embeddings into the binary tree and from it; and, for offspring supported on {1,2}, almost sure quasi-isometry together with an explicit exponential bound on the failure probability of a (D^2+3)-quasi-isometry. The statements are made in Challenge.lean over Mathlib alone and discharged by Solution.lean from four library targets.
